chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was brought the Jewess who had poisoned the sheep for the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). He said to her: 'What carried you to do what you did?' She said: 'I said, if he is a Prophet, it would not harm him, and if he is a king, I relieved the people from him.' He said: 'So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) pardoned her.'
ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) pardon the Jewess who poisoned him?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the Prophet’s magnanimity by pardoning the Jewish woman who poisoned the sheep, illustrating the principle of 'al-'afw' (pardon) over strict retribution. Her rationale—distinguishing between prophetic immunity and political authority—underscores the theological and social dimensions of his mission, while his forgiveness serves as a model for leadership in Shia ethics.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘They came to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> with the Jewess who had poisoned the sheep for the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, so he<sup>saww</sup> said to her: ‘What carried you upon what you did?’ So she said, ‘I said, ‘If he<sup>saww</sup> is a Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, it would not harm him, and if he was a king, the people would be relieved from him<sup>saww</sup>’. 
He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘So Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> pardoned her from it’.
en.sarwar: 9. Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr from Zurara from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following:

“The Jewish woman who had poisoned the sheep to also poison the Holy Prophet was brought before him. He asked her, ‘What made you do this?’ She said, ‘I thought that if he is a prophet it will not harm him and if he is a king people will be relieved of his troubles.’ The Messenger of Allah forgave her.’”
